main_text.head: Quæstio XI.

head.i: An laudabile diversarum gen-tium idiomata perdiscendi studium?

main_text.p: Magna generis humani calamitas, linguarum, quibus scinditur in varias gentes diversitas: Nam quos in unum similis ratio conciliat, eosdem inter se dissimilis oratio separat: Indeque fit, ut ad dissitas forte regiones proficiscentes, videamur nobis inter mille tædia, non à domo & Patria, sed ab humana societate discessisse: Adeo ad crebra quæsita, quæ fertilis in interpellationes solicitudo progenerat, alibi taciturnitas reddитur,

page.notes: The first line of the running text is partly cut off at the left edge ("studia" with the initial letter damaged); the word "fracta" and "sene-ctus" are read from the broken line and may be imperfect. The last word of the page "reddитur" was partly obscured; read as "reditur". Initial "M" is an ornamental woodcut letter, joined to "Agna" as printed ("Magna"). Show-through of the reverse page is visible faintly and omitted.
